transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because the clinic for this logistics job told me my weight was too low for them to clear me. I don’t really see it that way, though. To me I just look lean, like someone who can work and stay quick on his feet.
Can you tell me a bit about your eating habits lately—have you been eating regular meals, or have you been skipping meals or eating less than usual?

Most days I keep it pretty light. Black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or some tuna if I feel like I need something. If I’m not working a shift moving freight, I usually tell myself I don’t really need a full meal.
Can you tell me approximately how much you weigh now, and has your weight changed significantly in the past few months?

I don’t know the exact number right now. The clinic for that logistics job just said it was too low to clear me. I mean, I don’t really see it as a problem—I just look lean to me, like I’m ready to work and stay quick on my feet.
Can you tell me how much you currently weigh, in pounds or kilograms?
I don’t have the exact number on me. The job clinic just told me it was too low for them to clear me. I know that’s what they said, but I still feel like I just look lean, not unhealthy.
Can you tell me your current weight in pounds or kilograms?

I’m sorry, I don’t have the exact number. What I know is the job clinic said it was too low to clear me for the logistics work. To me, I just look lean, like I’m ready to work and stay quick on my feet.
Can you tell me your current weight in kilograms?
I don’t know the kilogram number. Like I said, the job clinic just told me my weight was too low to clear me. I still think I look lean, more like I’m fit for the logistics work and quick on my feet.
Can you tell me your height so I can get a better understanding of your body mass index?

I’m not sure of the exact height number either. The main thing is the job clinic said my weight was too low to clear me for the logistics work, though to me I just look lean—like I can stay quick on my feet.
Can you tell me your current weight in kilograms?

I still don’t have the kilogram number. All I really know is they said at the logistics job clinic that my weight was too low to clear me. I don’t see it that way exactly—I just think I look lean, like I can move quick and do the work.
Can you tell me your current weight in kilograms?

I really don’t know the number in kilograms. What I know is the clinic for the logistics job said my weight was too low to clear me. I don’t feel like I look too low, though—I just look lean to me, like I’m ready to work and stay quick on my feet.
Can you estimate your current Body Mass Index (BMI) or provide both your height and weight so I can calculate it?

I don’t have the BMI number, and I don’t really have the height and weight to give you right now. What I can tell you is I’m here because the logistics job clinic said my weight was too low to clear me. To me, I just look lean—like I’m ready to work and stay quick on my feet.
Can you tell me your height and weight in feet/inches and pounds so I can calculate your Body Mass Index (BMI)?

I don’t have the feet-and-inches or pounds numbers to give you right now. The reason I’m here is because that clinic for the logistics job said my weight was too low to clear me. I mean, I don’t really see it that way—I just look lean to me, like I can still work and move quick.

Has your low weight been intentional, or have you been losing weight without trying? If unintentional, have you experienced changes in appetite, gastrointestinal issues, or felt unusually hyperactive or restless?

I guess it’s more intentional than not. Most days I keep it pretty light—black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or a little tuna. And if I’m not moving freight that day, I tell myself I don’t really need a full meal.
Can you tell me why you choose to keep your weight low—do you have concerns about your body shape or weight, or is it more related to your job requirements or lifestyle?

It’s partly the work, I guess, but if I’m being honest it’s more how I see myself. When I look in the mirror, especially around my stomach and waist, I feel like I need to stay smaller and tight-looking. If I don’t, I feel like I’m not the disciplined guy I used to be on the warehouse floor.
Do you ever feel intense anxiety or fear about gaining weight or becoming larger, even if others might not see you that way?

Yeah… I do. If I eat something like rice or bread, or anything greasy, it gets in my head that it’s going to sit on me right away. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale, or see how my belt feels, just to make sure I didn’t let myself go.
Have you ever found yourself restricting your food intake even when you're hungry, or avoiding eating certain foods because you're afraid they'll make you gain weight?

Yeah. I do that a lot. Even if I’m hungry, most days I’ll just stick with black coffee, maybe a boiled egg or some tuna. And if I’m not on a shift moving freight, I tell myself I don’t really need a real meal anyway.
